analysis.title: Marketcolour + Memory / Earnings (Ioannis Blekos, GS Sales & Trading)
key_insights: US equities closed higher on 11/11 while the bond market was closed for Veterans Day. SPX +131bps to 7619, NDX +160bps to 25466 (back above its 200-dma and pre-election levels), DJIA +49bps to 52486, VIX -10% to 17.48. 9 of 11 sectors rose, Tech +390bps, Energy +205bps, Discretionary -23bps.
Semis are up nearly 20% from the local lows. GS attributes the move to cleaner positioning, vol resetting lower and election narratives being 'digested'.
Retail engaged: the GS Retail Favorite basket rose +495bps, its third best day in three years.
In Europe, EU Semis (GSSBSEMI) rose +5.6% and Electricals (GSXEACDC) rose +2.9%, on course for their best week since June. Defense (GSSBDEFE) fell -2.5%, under pressure again.
Nvidia closed with a 14-day RSI of about 24, the lowest since mid-2019, when NVDA was a roughly $100bn market cap stock.

Data center ballot measures: 41 were on the ballot and the pro-restriction side won nearly all. Half were in Ohio, and Maine, Illinois and Kansas account for nearly all the rest. All concerned individual towns, not counties or states. GS reads this as voters having a clear opinion when asked but not thinking about the issue otherwise.

A NY Times poll taken just before the election, asking voters to name their most important issue, is cited as further evidence that the public is not focused on data centers, despite Texas and Ohio being the center of the political debate.

Memory bull case (MU, SNDK, HDDs): stocks trade at 2-4x forward P/E and approach tangible book value, are just starting capital return programs (focus on MU earnings), have firm and rising spot prices (especially DRAM), and have guided to favorable supply/demand through 2027+.

Memory bear case: the market is nervous about 'over-earning' given the size of ASP tailwinds early in the cycle, especially if the build cycle becomes less linear. Supply-side unknowns remain (new entrants), and low P/E multiples in cycles are as much a bear case as a bull case.

Hedge fund performance: Systematic L/S managers rose 1.25%, a +2.6 SD move, with about 3/4 of funds up and the best day since June. Fundamentals rose 0.4% (+1.3% MTD) and Multi-Strats 0.7% (+0.2% MTD).

Siemens Q4 was a small beat with guidance ahead, and positioning was light. Group orders +58% were a massive beat, mainly from Mobility. Digital Industries (DI) orders +15% vs consensus +2%, Smart Infrastructure (SI) +39% vs +23%, organic sales growth +10% vs +8.5%. Adj EBITA beat by 2%, with SI helped by tariff refunds.

Siemens margins beat in all core divisions: DI 20.9% vs consensus 18.9%, SI 20.3% vs 19.5%, Mobility 9.5% vs 8.7%. Guidance is +9-11% group growth (consensus 8.5%), DI 8-12% (consensus +8%) and SI 11-13% (consensus 11%).

Siemens Energy (Buy, PT EUR200, 50% upside): new guidance is a 7% upgrade to Visible Alpha consensus profit before special items at the midpoint, 16% at the top end. The range implies margin before special items grows 6x by FY2030 vs FY2025, leaving the stock at 4-5x 2030 EV/EBITDA.

PGHN and TKO are rated Sell. For PGHN, GS sees downside risk to gross inflows and recurring fee economics. For TKO, strong relative share-price performance contrasts with weaker near-term fundraising. GS expects fundraising to stay subdued through 2027 and early 2028, and roll-off of private equity catch-up fees is a further headwind to FRE margin progression.

Allianz 3Q26 (Buy, PT EUR465): group operating profit beat company-collected consensus by 10%, driven by a 4% P&C beat, an 18% Asset Management beat and lower corporate costs. The P&C beat came from higher investment income, with the combined ratio and insurance revenue in line. The attritional loss ratio is about 80bps worse than consensus, including elevated weather and large losses about 90bps above normal.

Zurich 3Q26 P&C GWP +4% y/y and insurance revenue +7%. GWP was broadly in line with GS expectations and insurance revenue about 2% higher. Implied underlying GWP growth of 7% compares with GS's 4.5% estimate, on better price (1.0% vs -0.2%) and volume (6% vs 4.7%). EMEA was strongest and North America weaker (+0.1% vs 3%).

Munich Re: the bottom line and new guidance were already known, so the focus is on details. GS expects bears to point to the P&C Re undiscounted normalized combined ratio missing by 1.8ppts, with consensus looking too high for next year on that line. GS sees the stock down 1-2%.

Rolls-Royce trading statement was in line. EFH run-rating is toward the lower end of guidance, with financial guidance unchanged. Mid-term targets will be revisited in February, and there is a new interim buyback of £1.5bn to complete by FY27 results. The previous £2.5bn is nearly complete, so the total buyback by end-February will be £4bn out of the original £7-9bn commitment by 2028. GS indicates the stock +1%.
